assets.title: Percent for Art Locations
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Arts, Culture and the Creative Economy (Creative Philadelphia)
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: Artworks commissioned under the City's Percent for Art program; only status 'Active' kept (works listed as 'Inaccessible' or 'In Progress' left out). Polygon footprints placed as a point inside the footprint.

assets.title: PPR Art and Monuments
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: Sculpture, fountains and monuments in the Parks & Recreation collection (inventory points). No OpenDataPhilly page was found for this layer; landing link is the City's ArcGIS item.

assets.title: City Landmarks (points)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Innovation and Technology (CityGeo)
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: The City's basemap landmark points, limited to the subtypes that are civic or cultural (monuments, statues and fountains, murals, entertainment venues, historic sites, places of worship); zoo exhibit points, guard boxes and ruins, archived and non-public points left out. Last edited 2020, so recent changes may be missing.

assets.title: City Facilities (Master Facilities Database) — civic and cultural subset
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Public Property
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: Public-facing City assets only: museum buildings (arts_culture), City-owned historic houses (historic; guard boxes, ruins, springhouses and other outbuildings dropped) and City service offices such as L&I district offices and the Public Safety Services Campus (civic_safety). Inactive and not-public assets dropped; shelters and supportive housing deliberately left out; fire and police stations come from their own layers; recreation, library and health buildings belong to other domains.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap: museums, galleries, theaters, arts centers, public art
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: OSM tourism=museum|gallery|artwork|zoo and amenity=arts_centre|theatre|cinema|music_venue, plus community centres tagged or named as cultural centres. Fills gaps in the official layers (no machine-readable Mural Arts inventory is published); OSM mural coverage is partial and many artworks are unnamed.

assets.title: Philadelphia Register of Historic Places — individually designated properties
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Philadelphia Historical Commission
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: Properties individually designated on the Philadelphia Register, as a point inside each parcel; the layer carries addresses, not names, so the address is the name. Properties that are only contributing to a historic district are summarised by the district points (phl_historic_districts), except a school site itself, which is kept and marked 'This school site'.

assets.title: Philadelphia Register historic districts (one point per district)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Philadelphia Historical Commission
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: One point per local historic district (including thematic districts) that reaches within 1.5 miles of a site, placed inside the part of the district nearest that site; detail gives the designation date (from the property records when the district layer has none or its 1/1/3000 placeholder) and the number of Register properties in the district.

assets.title: National Register of Historic Places (points)
assets.publisher: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places
assets.notes: Public, non-restricted National Register listings with status 'Listed' (removed listings dropped); districts appear as a single point. Website is the National Archives catalog record of the nomination. Five of the six school buildings are listed (Robeson is not) and are marked 'This school site'.

assets.title: Pennsylvania Historical Markers
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (data.pa.gov)
assets.notes: PHMC historical markers in Philadelphia at the coordinates PHMC publishes; markers whose status is 'True' (known missing) left out.

assets.title: Police Stations (district headquarters)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Philadelphia Police Department
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: Police district headquarters; the published phone has no area code, so 215 was added. Some locations are given as intersections.

assets.title: Fire Department Facilities
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Philadelphia Fire Department
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: Fire stations named by the engine and ladder companies housed there; medic and battalion units in detail (the layer's special-unit codes are not explained by the publisher and were left out). Most locations are given as intersections.

assets.title: Polling Places
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, City Commissioners (Philadelphia County Board of Elections)
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: One point per polling place (divisions voting at the same place merged; ward-divisions in detail). Accessibility and parking codes spelled out from the City Commissioners' legend (vote.phila.gov polling place list). Polling places change between elections.

assets.title: Registered Community Organizations (office or meeting point)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Philadelphia City Planning Commission
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: Each RCO placed at its organization address with the US Census geocoder; when that is a PO box, cannot be matched, or is the same as a contact person's own address (and not a suite or floor in an office building), its meeting place is used instead, and failing both a point inside its boundary (detail says which). Only name, type, website and which school sites the boundary covers are kept; no contact names, e-mails or phones.

assets.title: Neighborhood Advisory Committees (offices)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Division of Housing and Community Development
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: NAC office locations; organization phone and website kept, coordinator names and e-mails not requested.

assets.title: PPR Friends Groups
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data terms of use (https://metadata.phila.gov/#help/help-faqs/what-are-the-terms-of-use/)
assets.notes: Volunteer friends groups, placed at the park they support; contact e-mails not requested.

assets.title: PACDC member CDCs
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Association of Community Development Corporations (PACDC)
assets.license: No license stated; published by PACDC as its public member map
assets.notes: The 'CDC Members' layer of PACDC's public member map (Associate Members such as banks and consultants left out), placed with the US Census geocoder from the street address PACDC lists. Organization phone and website kept. Not matched by the geocoder: Called To Serve CDC, Frankford CDC, Cliveden of the National Trust.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap: community centers and social clubs
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: OSM amenity=community_centre|social_centre that are not City-run and not youth, older-adult or recreation centres (those belong to other categories and were left out). Non-City community centres are filed under community_orgs as community-run places; cultural centres went to arts_culture.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap: places of worship
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: OSM amenity=place_of_worship (nodes, ways and relations, placed at the feature or its centre); religion and denomination from OSM tags in detail. Unnamed features kept with an empty name. No official citywide inventory of congregations is published.

assets.title: FDIC-Insured Bank Branch Locations
assets.publisher: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) BankFind Suite
assets.notes: All FDIC-insured bank offices in Philadelphia, Montgomery and Delaware counties within 1.5 mi of a site; kept full-service brick-and-mortar/retail offices and limited-service drive-thru/retail facilities, dropped trust, administrative, messenger, mobile/seasonal and loan-production offices. Website is the institution's FDIC-listed web address.

assets.title: Credit Union Offices (NCUA Credit Union Locator)
assets.publisher: National Credit Union Administration (NCUA)
assets.notes: Federally insured credit union sites returned by NCUA's locator within 2 mi of each site address, kept within 1.5 mi; ATM-only sites dropped. Many are workplace or church-based credit unions with restricted membership; the field of membership is in the detail line. Credit union type and website from NCUA's credit union profile.

assets.title: PA CareerLink Philadelphia Centers and Outreach Sites
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Works, Inc. (PA CareerLink® Philadelphia)
assets.license: Published on pacareerlinkphl.org; no open license stated
assets.notes: Marker list behind the 'Career Centers' map on PA CareerLink Philadelphia's contact page: the four full-time comprehensive centers, the Northeast Hub, part-time outreach sites (mostly in Free Library branches) and partner sites. Used instead of data.pa.gov's CareerLink Locations (6p38-7dgx, last updated 2022), which still lists the old West Philadelphia address.

assets.title: Workforce and Employment Resources (Office of Black Male Engagement Directory)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Black Male Engagement
assets.license: City of Philadelphia open data (OpenDataPhilly terms of use)
assets.notes: Organizations in the City's public resource directory (public_yn = Y) whose listed services include workforce development or employment; most are multi-service nonprofits rather than job centers. Emails dropped.

assets.title: Schools (district, charter, private, Archdiocese)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Planning and Development
assets.notes: All school points in the City layer; the candidate schools themselves were left out (Academy for the Middle Years at Northwest, Fitler Academics Plus School, General Louis Wagner School, Paul Robeson High School for Human Services, Rudolph Blankenburg School, Samuel Pennypacker School). Enrollment and grades are as the City layer states them; the layer covers Philadelphia only.

assets.title: Public school locations outside Philadelphia, 2024-25 (NCES Common Core of Data)
assets.publisher: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics (EDGE / CCD)
assets.notes: Only schools outside Philadelphia County (the City Schools layer stops at the city line); full-time virtual schools and closed schools were left out.

assets.title: Private school locations, 2023-24 (NCES Private School Survey), gap fill
assets.publisher: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics (EDGE / PSS)
assets.notes: Only private schools the City Schools layer does not have: those outside Philadelphia, and Philadelphia schools with no City point of a similar name within 400 m (or any school within 80 m). The survey lists schools teaching at least one of grades K-12 (some may have closed since 2023-24); this layer gives no grade span or enrollment.

assets.title: Child care providers including early learning programs (PA DHS certified facilities)
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, Office of Child Development and Early Learning (OCDEL)
assets.notes: Certified child care centers, group homes and family homes, plus federal Head Start locations the list carries as provider type 'Other'; 2 other 'Other' rows (private academic school programs) and the school-age-only providers were left out (the latter are in pa_dhs_school_age_child_care). Family and group homes are residences: facility name and address as published, no phone, no owner names.

assets.title: School-age child care providers (PA DHS certified, school-age only)
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, Office of Child Development and Early Learning (OCDEL)
assets.notes: Providers in the same PA DHS list whose capacity is 'School Age Provider', i.e. licensed before/after-school programs for school-age children only; kept as out-of-school-time assets.

assets.title: PHLpreK program sites, FY25 enrollment
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Children and Families (PHLpreK), published by PhillyStat 360
assets.license: Not stated on the item (public City of Philadelphia ArcGIS Online layer)
assets.data_date: FY25 slots and enrollment as of 2024-12-02 (layer last edited 2024-12-09)
assets.notes: Every PHLpreK provider site in the layer. It is the most recent public PHLpreK site list found (FY25); sites added or dropped since then are not reflected.

assets.title: Pre-K Counts and Head Start Supplemental Assistance Program (HSSAP) funded locations
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Education, Office of Child Development and Early Learning (OCDEL)
assets.notes: Only the latest funding quarter; one point per location, with its Pre-K Counts and HSSAP slots combined. Includes School District of Philadelphia classrooms that are not DHS-licensed child care.

assets.title: School District of Philadelphia pre-K sites (Head Start, Bright Futures, partners), SY 2024-2025
assets.publisher: School District of Philadelphia, Office of Research and Evaluation
assets.license: School District of Philadelphia open data (terms at philasd.org/research)
assets.notes: District pre-K list (district-run Head Start / Bright Futures classrooms and community partner sites). The file has addresses only; points were geocoded with the City's AIS address service (Census geocoder as fallback).

assets.title: Free Library of Philadelphia locations
assets.publisher: Free Library of Philadelphia, published by the City of Philadelphia (maps.phl.data)
assets.notes: Active Free Library locations (the City's current 'library_locations' layer; the older 'Free_Library_Locations' layer was last edited in 2018 and was not used).

assets.title: Public libraries outside the Free Library system (PA 'Services Near You': Public Library layer)
assets.publisher: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania (Department of Education, Office of Commonwealth Libraries, via data.pa.gov)
assets.notes: Public libraries in the Commonwealth list that are not Free Library branches (those within 150 m of a Free Library location were dropped as duplicates); also dropped: Hosting Solutions & Library Consulting (HSLC) (a library-services office).

assets.title: Out-of-school-time (OST) program sites, FY24
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Children and Families (OST)
assets.license: Not stated on the item (public City of Philadelphia ArcGIS Online layer)
assets.data_date: FY24 (2023-24) program year; layer last edited 2023-09-27
assets.notes: Publicly funded after-school sites (City DHS/OCF, School District, federal 21st CCLC, Mural Arts) as the City listed them for FY24; the newest public OST site list found (FY25/26 layers in the City's OST map are not public). Sites marked 'TBD new RFP' had funded slots but no provider yet.

assets.title: Police Athletic League (PAL) Centers
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Police Department
assets.notes: All PAL centers in the layer; the center director's name in the source was not kept.

assets.title: Postsecondary institution locations, 2025-26 (NCES EDGE / IPEDS)
assets.publisher: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics (EDGE / IPEDS)
assets.notes: One point per IPEDS institution (its main address), so branch campuses are not here (see pa_pde_higher_ed_campuses). The kind is read from the institution name.

assets.title: PA higher education institutions by sector (campus locations)
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Education
assets.notes: Full-service college locations (main campuses, branch campuses and off-campus operations such as the Community College of Philadelphia regional centers); limited instructional sites are not in this list.

assets.title: Universities and Colleges (City building inventory, grouped into campus points)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Planning and Development
assets.notes: The source has one polygon per college building. Buildings of the same institution within ~200 m of each other inside the study area were grouped into one point (at the building nearest the group's center); single buildings keep their name.

assets.title: Youth centers, YMCA / YWCA, Boys & Girls Clubs, scouting (OpenStreetMap)
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: OSM fills the gap where no official list exists (YMCA / Boys & Girls Club branches, youth centers): features tagged as youth centres or scouting, or named YMCA, YWCA, Boys & Girls Club, PAL, Youth or Teen; schools, churches, shelters, treatment and justice facilities, playgrounds and courts were left out. Coverage depends on volunteer mapping.

assets.title: Colleges and universities (OpenStreetMap)
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: Named features tagged amenity=college or amenity=university (campus outlines become a point inside them). Used only to fill gaps in the NCES / PDE / City lists; OSM 'college' also covers some trade and career schools.

assets.title: Philadelphia Free Food and Meal Sites
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Children and Families (with Philabundance, SHARE and partner food banks)
assets.notes: Active food pantries, free grocery sites, community fridges and free meal sites only. Excluded: Office of Homeless Services meal sites (shelter locations), WIC / BenePhilly / Neighborhood Community Action Center benefit sites (social services) and PCA / PPR senior meal sites (older adults), plus permanently closed sites. Food-bank homepages given as a site's website are left blank. Every address was geocoded (City AIS, Census fallback): citywide 55 source points lying more than 250 m from their own address (mostly Caring for Friends sites) were moved to the address; 2 addresses could not be geocoded and keep the source point.

assets.title: Farmers' Market Locations
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia (compiled from market managers and operators)
assets.notes: All listed markets; schedule, season and SNAP / FMNP / Philly Food Bucks acceptance in detail. Operator name and phone kept only when the operator is an organisation (individual farmers' names and phones are left out).

assets.title: SNAP Retailer Locator: authorized retailers
assets.publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food and Nutrition Service (SNAP Retailer Policy and Management Division)
assets.license: U.S. Government work; no license stated on the item
assets.data_date: layer last edited 2026-11-05 (USDA updates every 2 weeks)
assets.notes: Kept USDA store types Supermarket, Super Store, Grocery Store, Specialty Store and Farmers and Markets; dropped Convenience Store and Other (pharmacies, dollar and gas-station stores). Store type is USDA's classification; many small 'Grocery Store' retailers are corner stores with limited fresh food.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap supermarkets, grocery stores and produce markets
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: shop=supermarket, greengrocer and grocery (convenience stores skipped). Gap filler for the USDA list; OSM coverage of small stores is incomplete.

assets.title: PHS Community Garden Program: PHS- and NGT-supported gardens (current)
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Horticultural Society (PHS), with Neighborhood Gardens Trust (NGT)
assets.license: No license stated; public layer shared by PHS
assets.notes: Active gardens in PHS's Community Garden Program ('CGP active gardens'). The current layer has no addresses, so the address comes from PHS's December 2022 supported-gardens layer when a garden point lies within 40 m.

assets.title: Registered Community Gardens
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation, Urban Agriculture Team
assets.notes: Active gardens registered with PPR's Urban Agriculture Team (a short citywide list of 23; most community gardens are not registered). Contact emails left out.

assets.title: Urban Agriculture Projects
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation (Farm Philly)
assets.notes: Active urban agriculture projects on PPR sites (10 citywide). Contact emails left out.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap community gardens and urban farms
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: landuse=allotments (community garden), landuse=farmland / farmyard (urban farm) and leisure=garden with garden:type=community. Polygons placed at a point inside; unnamed features are labelled by type.

assets.title: PPR Properties (parks as points)
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.notes: One point inside each PPR property polygon (inside the part that lies within 1.5 mi of a site for large parks); acreage is the whole property. Dropped traffic islands / medians, pathways, internal operational sites and older-adult-center properties; PPR garden / farm properties are tagged gardens_farms.

assets.title: Parks & Recreation Program Sites
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.notes: Recreation centers / staffed recreation sites, program pools and environmental education centers. Older adult centers (program_type OLDER_ADULT_CENTER) excluded for the health domain. Address taken from the PPR property the point sits in.

assets.title: PPR Playgrounds
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.notes: PPR play areas (grouped by age range). Play areas of the same park within 40 m are merged into one point with the count and age ranges in detail.

assets.title: PPR Spraygrounds
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.notes: Active spraygrounds and sprinklers only (status INACTIVE / UNKNOWN dropped).

assets.title: PPR Swimming Pools
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.notes: Active PPR pools (inactive pools dropped). Pool status is PPR's facility status, not this season's opening schedule.

assets.title: PPR Tennis Courts
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.notes: One record per court in the source; courts at the same park within 40 m are merged into one point with a count.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap courts, athletic fields, tracks, rinks and skateparks
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: leisure=pitch / track / ice_rink / skatepark, typed by sport; access=private / customers dropped, as are painted schoolyard games (four square, gaga). Adjacent same-type courts within 40 m merged with a count. Detail says whether the facility sits in a PPR park, on school grounds or on a college campus (school courts may not be open to the public). Fills the gap left by PPR, which publishes no ballfield / basketball court layer.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap parks, playgrounds and dog parks outside PPR property
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: Gap filler: named leisure=park / nature_reserve, leisure=playground and leisure=dog_park whose point lies outside every PPR property (playgrounds also > 60 m from a PPR play area); includes township parks across the city line, institutional and housing-site playgrounds. access=private / customers dropped; detail flags school grounds.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap trailheads
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors (via Overpass API)
assets.notes: highway=trailhead nodes (mostly Wissahickon Valley Park entrances). No official City trailhead point layer exists; PPR publishes trails only as lines.

assets.title: Health Centers
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Public Health
assets.notes: City health centers (PDPH) and the community health centers the City lists. Quality Community Health Care (QCHC) sites appear here but not in HRSA's current FQHC list, so check that they still operate.

assets.title: Philadelphia Hospitals
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Public Health
assets.notes: All hospitals on the City list. Kirkbride Center (111 N 49th St, mostly residential addiction treatment) is left out under the no-addiction-residence rule. Some names predate mergers and closures; pa_doh_hospitals carries the current state licensure names.

assets.title: PA Department of Health Hospitals (DOH Hospitals 202511)
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Health (via PASDA)
assets.notes: Hospitals licensed by PA DOH. Private psychiatric hospitals licensed by PA DHS (e.g. Belmont, Friends) are not in this list; the City list has them. Executive names are not kept.

assets.title: Health Center Service Delivery and Look-Alike Sites
assets.publisher: U.S. Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Bureau of Primary Health Care
assets.notes: Active, permanent FQHC and look-alike service delivery sites; administrative-only offices, seasonal sites and mobile vans are left out, as are clinics inside shelters or residential treatment (Interim House West, Stenton Family Manor, PEC/HopePHL). School-based sites are kept and labeled.

assets.title: FindTreatment.gov behavioral health treatment facilities (outpatient)
assets.publisher: U.S. Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
assets.notes: Mental health and substance use facilities that offer outpatient care. Any facility that also offers residential or 24-hour residential treatment is left out (no addiction-treatment residences); facilities listed twice (MH and SUD) are merged.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap clinics, doctors, dentists and other health care
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors
assets.notes: amenity=clinic|doctors|dentist and healthcare=* points with a name. Hospitals and pharmacies are in their own datasets; alternative medicine, home-care agencies, individual psychotherapists, 'rehabilitation' and anything named for addiction / recovery treatment are left out. Coverage is uneven: OSM misses many small practices.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap pharmacies
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors
assets.notes: amenity=pharmacy, healthcare=pharmacy and shop=chemist. Rite Aid is dropped (all stores closed in 2025). OSM may still show chain stores closed in 2024-26 and misses independents; see cms_nppes_pharmacies.

assets.title: NPPES NPI Registry: community / retail pharmacies in Philadelphia
assets.publisher: U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), National Plan and Provider Enumeration System
assets.notes: Organization NPIs whose primary taxonomy is community/retail pharmacy, at their practice location, geocoded with the City's AIS. NPIs are rarely deactivated when a store closes, so Rite Aid is dropped and records not updated in the last five years are skipped; the rest are likely but not certain to be open.

assets.title: PCA Senior Centers
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Corporation for Aging (geocoded by the City of Philadelphia)
assets.license: Not stated (City of Philadelphia ArcGIS Online item)
assets.notes: Senior community centers and PHA satellite sites from PCA's Find a Senior Center list, as geocoded by the City.

assets.title: Parks & Recreation Program Sites: older adult centers
assets.publisher: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
assets.notes: PPR program sites with program_type = OLDER_ADULT_CENTER (the value the layer uses now; older extracts used PPR_OAC). The layer has no street address.

assets.title: LIFE (Living Independence for the Elderly) provider centers
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, Office of Long-Term Living
assets.license: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania web page (no open license stated)
assets.notes: Philadelphia LIFE (PACE) centers from the provider table on the DHS page, geocoded with the City's AIS. LIFE centers are the adult day health sites of the program.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap senior centers and adult day centers
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors
assets.notes: Named senior / older adult centers, senior service agencies and adult day centers. Senior housing, nursing homes and assisted living are left out (residences).

assets.title: Women, Infants & Children (WIC) Offices
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Public Health
assets.notes: All WIC offices in the City list.

assets.title: Neighborhood Resources (Neighborhood Energy Centers and Housing Counseling Agencies)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Planning and Development, Division of Housing and Community Development
assets.notes: Agencies flagged as a Neighborhood Energy Center (utility bill help, ECA) or a City-funded housing counseling agency. NAC-only offices are left to community_orgs. This layer supersedes the separate Neighborhood_Energy_Centers and HousingCounselingAgencies layers. Contact names and e-mails are not kept.

assets.title: HUD-approved Housing Counseling Agencies
assets.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
assets.notes: HUD-approved agencies returned by HUD's search-by-location API within 2 miles of each site, kept within 1.5 miles. Agency phone and website only; staff e-mails are not kept.

assets.title: County Assistance Office Current Statewide Human Services
assets.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (via data.pa.gov)
assets.license: Public Domain U.S. Government (as labeled on data.pa.gov)
assets.notes: DHS County Assistance Offices (SNAP / 'food stamps', cash assistance, Medical Assistance, LIHEAP). District offices that share a building are merged into one point. The rows were last updated in 2022.

assets.title: Healthy Start Community Resource Centers
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Public Health
assets.notes: PDPH-affiliated Healthy Start family resource centers (prenatal and early-childhood family support).

assets.title: Black Male Engagement Resources (legal and family support entries)
assets.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Black Male Engagement
assets.license: Not stated (City of Philadelphia ArcGIS Online item)
assets.notes: Only entries offering legal services or fatherhood / family support; this is the only official geocoded source found for legal aid offices. Shelters, victim services and hospital programs are left out; e-mails are not kept.

assets.title: OpenStreetMap social service offices
assets.publisher: OpenStreetMap contributors
assets.notes: Gap fill only: Social Security and VA benefits offices, legal aid, social_facility=outreach|advice and family service agencies. County Assistance and WIC offices come from the official datasets. Shelters, group homes, recovery residences and victim / domestic-violence services are left out.

methods.title: What the map is for
methods.text: An inventory of what exists around each site, to inform how Wagner and Blankenburg could be reused. It does not rank sites or recommend uses; empty categories are reported as facts, not as needs.

methods.title: Collection
methods.text: Five inventories (education, health and social services, food and open space, civic and culture, economy and housing) were pulled from the publishers listed under Asset sources, within 1.5 miles of each of the six schools (community organizations within 2 miles). Official City, Commonwealth and federal sources come first; OpenStreetMap fills kinds the official sources do not cover, and is labelled as such.

methods.title: De-duplication
methods.text: The same kind of place listed by two sources (same or very similar name within about 500 m, or an unnamed record within 80 m) is counted once, keeping the official source's record.

methods.title: Distances and the radius
methods.text: Distances are straight lines from the school (the centroid of its building parcel), shown in miles; walk times assume the studio's pace of 80 m a minute. The radius slider changes the ring, the counts and the within-radius filter; nothing is inventoried beyond 1.5 miles.

methods.title: 15-minute walk
methods.text: Areas reachable along the OpenStreetMap walk network in 5, 10 and 15 minutes from the street corner nearest the school, with reachable streets widened 25 m and small enclosed gaps filled; residents from 2020 Census blocks. Wagner and Blankenburg use the studio's own walk areas; the other four use the same method.

methods.title: Study-area profile
methods.text: Census tract counts from the ACS 2020–2024 5-year estimates, each weighted by the share of the tract's 2020 residents living within half a mile of the school (block population); medians by the aggregate median method. Rebuilding Wagner and Blankenburg this way reproduces the studio's published figures.

methods.title: Catchments and building ratings
methods.text: Attendance boundaries are the School District's 2024 catchments (all grades whose assignment is the school). Building condition, program, utilization and vulnerability ratings are the District's Facilities Master Plan scores as recorded in the studio's site list.

methods.title: Privacy and safety
methods.text: No private individuals: RCO contact names, emails and phones are left out, as are domestic-violence shelters, residential treatment sites and other locations sources mark confidential. Family child care homes appear as the State lists them.

methods.title: Caveats
methods.text: Open data lags reality: places close and open, OpenStreetMap coverage is uneven, and some City layers carry older survey dates (see each source's data date). Census tract estimates carry wide margins of error. Check anything decisive on the ground.
